Robust quadratic model of track length versus replication percentage

Source: R/track_velocity.R
fit_track_velocity_linear.Rd

Fit log_length ~ rep_percent + I(rep_percent^2) with robustbase::lmrob() (plus lm() with a linear term and, optionally, a median regression with quantreg::rq()), predict on an even grid with confidence and prediction intervals, derive the length velocity exp(fit) * (b1 + 2 b2 x) and validate on a random hold-out split.

Usage

fit_track_velocity_linear(
  data,
  n_grid = 100L,
  level = 0.95,
  quantile = TRUE,
  holdout_prop = 0.5,
  seed = 2026L,
  fit_seed = NULL,
  positive_velocity_only = TRUE,
  min_cells = 20L,
  min_distinct = 8L,
  sort_by_rep = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

Output of summarize_track_lengths() (rep_percent, median_length, log_length).

n_grid

Number of prediction points (e.g. 100 or 200).

level

Confidence level of the intervals.

quantile

Logical; also fit the median regression (needs quantreg).

holdout_prop

Fraction of cells used for training in the hold-out validation (floor(holdout_prop * n)).

seed

Seed of the hold-out split.

fit_seed

NULL or a seed for the full-data fits (see Details).

positive_velocity_only

Logical; drop prediction rows with length_velocity <= 0.

min_cells, min_distinct

Minimum number of cells and of distinct rep_percent values (e.g. 20 and 8).

sort_by_rep

Logical; sort the cells by rep_percent before fitting (default); FALSE keeps the input order. The order changes the hold-out split and the row order of data, and moves the lmrob() fits within its convergence tolerance.

Value

An object of class scrt_track_velocity (a list) with model = "linear", the fits fit_linear, fit_lmrob, fit_rq, data (with is_outlier = zero robustness weight), prediction, linear_residuals, robust_residuals, validation, validation_metrics (rmse, pseudo_r2, correlation), model_comparison (long table of the lmrob / rq predicted lengths), minimal_predicted_length (exp(b0 - b1^2 / (4 b2))) and rep_range.

Details

Cells with non-finite rep_percent or median_length, or median_length <= 0, are dropped and (with sort_by_rep = TRUE) the data are sorted by rep_percent. Intervals use qt((1 + level) / 2, df.residual) with the lmrob standard errors and residual scale.

lmrob() draws random subsamples for its initial estimate; with fit_seed = NULL the current random-number state is used, otherwise the fits run under withr::with_seed(fit_seed).

See also

fit_track_length_models(), fit_track_velocity_ode(), predict_rep_percent()
